import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 4

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture4

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 4](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

If `G` is a connected graph then the maximum number of leaves over all spanning
trees satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ NG(G) - 1` where `NG(G)` is the minimal neighbourhood
size of a non-edge of `G`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture4 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nontrivial α] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    NG G - 1 ≤ Ls G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture4

reformulations.difference: The Lean theorem assumes Nontrivial α and uses NG's convention NG(K_n) = n when there are no nonedges. The source says 'simple connected graph' and takes a minimum over nonedges without specifying an empty-minimum convention.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For graphs having a nonedge, NG is exactly the source's minimum neighborhood-union cardinality. A graph without nonedges is complete; its spanning star has at least n−1 leaves for n≥2, so the additional complete-graph cases are automatically true with NG(K_n)=n. The only connected graph excluded by Nontrivial is the singleton, where NG=1 and Ls=0, giving 0≤0. Thus these choices do not change the mathematical claim. The scratch file proves both nonedge_restriction_iff and nontrivial_restriction_iff, independently of the conjecture.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 4 and its status, archived 26 July 2026: https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html

WOWII definitions and references, especially defEntry(1), defEntry(8), defEntry(20), and conjEntry(4): https://web.archive.org/web/20240726225301id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowii/wowIIdefs.js
E. DeLaVina, original November 1996 list, pp. 1–2, including Conjecture 4 and its proof: https://web.archive.org/web/20230703190700id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII.pdf

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states Conjecture 4. The source marks it T (true), credits DeLaVina in 1996, and supplies the original proof, agreeing with research solved. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/checks.lean compile without errors or sorryAx dependencies: they establish that Ls's finite supremum is attained and equivalent to the expected spanning-tree existence statement, verify empty/singleton cases and NG(K₂)=Ls(K₂)=2, and prove the complete-graph bound. An independent exhaustive computation found no violations among connected labeled graphs through six vertices. Archived sources were used because the live HTTPS endpoint was unreachable. The reviewed file matches its committed contents.
